title: Thermal-aware microbatch bundling and conservative clock fallback for mixed-sku MIG fleets
creator: Diego Alvarez
description:
Problem statement: On mixed-SKU MIG-hosted inference clusters (H100/L40S with some A10 fallbacks) we observe intermittent prefill tail-latency spikes correlated with thermal headroom reductions and aggressive clock stepping. These manifest as 95/99p latency degradations during sustained workloads and cause cascading queue piles that increase cost and SLO violations.

Goal: Implement a thermal-headroom-aware microbatch bundling + conservative clock fallback policy that: (1) dynamically adjusts microbatch bundling across MIG slices to reduce instantaneous power spikes, (2) selects kernels with lower clock-sensitivity (e.g., attention tiling variants, sparsity-friendly kernels, or lower-precision microkernels) when headroom is low, and (3) gracefully falls back to quantized/A10-compatible kernels when NVIDIA clocks fall below threshold. The solution should preserve throughput where possible and avoid large latency regressions for p50/p90 while improving p95/p99 stability.

Design summary:
- Thermal estimator: aggregate per-GPU telemetry (SM utilization, power draw, GPU temp gradient, NVML clock limits) into a short-window thermal headroom score (0..1). Implement estimator in runtime telemetry agent with 2s resolution.
- Bundling heuristic: when headroom < 0.45, prefer microbatch bundles that spread concurrent token-generation across MIG slices (soft spread) instead of coalescing into a single high-power bundle. Add a hysteresis window to avoid oscillation.
- Kernel selection policy: annotate kernel candidates with volatility metadata (clock-sensitive | clock-robust). Extend kernel ranking to add a thermal penalty term; when headroom < threshold, prefer clock-robust kernels even if slightly more expensive token-wise.
- Conservative clock fallback: if clocks step down beyond a measured delta (e.g., sustained GPU core clock drop >10% for 10s), transparently route new sessions to lower-sensitivity model variants / quantized kernels (A10-compat) with rapid warmup prefill. Maintain KV cache compatibility via pinned model-version mapping.
- Prefill scheduling: delay non-critical prefill work and stagger prefill starts across tenants when headroom is low. Implement prioritized queueing for latency-critical routes.
- Rollout: canary on a small Dedicated pool (H100-heavy), then extended canary on mixed-sku test fleet, monitor p95/p99 latency, GPU power and thermostat events, and customer error rates.

Acceptance criteria:
- p95/p99 token generation latency improves or reduces variance by at least 30% during a synthetic sustained workload that induces thermal headroom dips.
- No regressions >5% in p50/p90 across normal workloads.
- Fallback switching completes within 3s of sustained clock drop detection and preserves KV cache semantics for live sessions.
- New telemetry dashboard shows thermal headroom, kernel-choice distributions, fallback events, and per-tenant SLO impacts.

Observability: Add new traces/tags: runtime.thermal_headroom, runtime.bundle_strategy, runtime.kernel_choice_hint, runtime.fallback_reason. Export events to console rollouts dashboard and include sampling for full-stack trace on fallback.

Telemetry experiments: run A/B where 50% of canary traffic uses the new policy and 50% uses current baseline; record token latency distributions, token/sec, GPU watt/s, and fallback frequency.

Operational concerns: ensure that the policy cannot continually route traffic to A10 or quantized variants and create accuracy regressions. Add guardrail config flags per-customer to disable automatic fallback.

Deliverables: implementation in runtime kernel-ranker + prefill scheduler, telemetry agent changes, console dashboard tiles, demo runbook and canary playbook, PR with performance benchmarks and synthetic workload scripts.

implementation_notes: Add thermal_headroom field to runtime telemetry proto; aim for 2s resolution and 10s decay half-life
Extend kernel metadata to include 'clock_sensitivity' tag and a numeric penalty weight
Prefill scheduler to support 'staggered' mode with tenant priorities
Fallback state machine persisted to local runtime state and events emitted for tracing
Guardrails: per-tenant opt-out flag and soft-limit counters to prevent frequent fallback oscillation
